photos.habitat: Large permanent water bodies such as rybníky, jezera, and slow-moving potoky across eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Bullfrogs are named for their deep, resonant call that can be heard up to a quarter mile away. They are voracious predators that will eat almost anything they can swallow, including other frogs.

photos.habitat: Deciduous and mixed lesy near rybníky and potoky in eastern Severní Amerika. They spend most of their time underground.
photos.funFact: Spotted salamanders have a symbiotic relationship with algae that live in their egg masses, providing oxygen to developing embryos. They can regenerate lost limbs and tails.

photos.habitat: Wooded areas near rybníky, swamps, and marshes across eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Spring peepers are among the first frogs to call in spring, creating a chorus that can be heard from over a mile away. They can survive being frozen solid during winter.

photos.habitat: Forest floors under logs, rocks, and leaf litter in eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Red-backed salamanders are lungless and breathe entirely through their skin and mouth lining. They are territorial and will defend their small territories aggressively.

photos.habitat: lesy and woodlands near temporary pools across northern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Wood frogs can survive being frozen solid for months during winter. They produce glucose and urea as natural antifreeze to protect their vital organs.

photos.habitat: Tropical rainlesy near water sources in Střední Amerika.
photos.funFact: Red-eyed tree frogs have bright red eyes that startle predators. They can change color from bright green to dark brown depending on their mood and environment.

photos.habitat: rybníky, jezera, and slow potoky with aquatic vegetation across eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Eastern newts have a unique three-stage life cycle including an aquatic larva, terrestrial juvenile (eft), and aquatic adult. The bright orange eft stage can last 2-7 let on land.

photos.habitat: Tropical rainlesy of Colombia and Ecuador.
photos.funFact: Golden poison dart frogs are among the most toxic animals on Earth. One frog contains enough poison to kill 10 adult humans, but they're only toxic in the wild due to their diet.

photos.habitat: Lake Xochimilco and surrounding canals in Mexico City.
photos.funFact: Axolotls can regenerate entire limbs, organs, and even parts of their brain. They remain aquatic their entire lives and are critically endangered in the wild.

photos.habitat: Diverse habitats from lesy to travnaté oblasti near rybníky across Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Tiger salamanders are the largest terrestrial salamanders in Severní Amerika. They can live underground for let and emerge only to breed.

photos.habitat: Trees and shrubs near water in southeastern Spojené státy.
photos.funFact: Green tree frogs can change color from bright green to gray or brown. They have sticky toe pads that allow them to climb smooth surfaces like glass.

photos.habitat: Fast-flowing, rocky potoky in eastern Spojené státy.
photos.funFact: Hellbenders are Severní Amerika's largest salamanders and can live for decades. They breathe through their wrinkled skin and are indicators of clean water quality.

photos.habitat: Diverse habitats from rainlesy to urban areas, native to Central and Jižní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Cane toads are highly toxic and invasive in many countries. They can eat almost anything that fits in their mouth and have poison glands behind their eyes.

photos.habitat: Deciduous lesy near potoky in Europe.
photos.funFact: Fire salamanders have bright yellow markings that warn predators of their toxicity. They can live for decades and give birth to live larvae rather than laying eggs.

photos.habitat: Permanent water bodies including jezera, řeky, and potoky in eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Mudpuppies are fully aquatic salamanders that keep their external gills throughout their lives. They are active year-round, even under ice in winter.

photos.habitat: Tropical rainlesy near potoky in Central and Jižní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Glass frogs have transparent skin on their belly, allowing you to see their internal organs. Males guard their eggs and will fight off intruders.

photos.habitat: Underground burrows in tropical soils of Střední Amerika.
photos.funFact: Caecilians are worm-like amphibians that live underground. They are nearly blind and use chemical sensors to navigate and find prey in the soil.

photos.habitat: travnaté oblasti, prairies, and agricultural areas near temporary pools across central Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Chorus frogs are among the first to call in spring, creating loud choruses that can be heard from great distances. They can survive partial freezing.

photos.habitat: Deciduous and mixed lesy across eastern Spojené státy.
photos.funFact: Marbled salamanders breed in fall rather than spring. Females guard their eggs in dry pond beds until winter rains fill the pools and the eggs hatch.

photos.habitat: Cool, clear potoky and springs in eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Pickerel frogs produce toxic skin secretions that can kill other frogs in the same container. They have distinctive square spots arranged in two rows down their back.

photos.habitat: Sphagnum bogs and coniferous swamps in eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Four-toed salamanders are the only salamanders with a constriction at the base of their tail, allowing them to easily detach it when threatened.

photos.habitat: Trees and shrubs near water across eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Gray tree frogs can change color from gray to green to brown. They have a distinctive trill call and bright orange coloring on their inner thighs.

photos.habitat: Springs, potoky, and surrounding lesy in eastern Spojené státy.
photos.funFact: Red salamanders mimic the coloration of toxic red efts to avoid predation. They can live for over 20 let and are excellent indicators of water quality.

photos.habitat: Trees and shrubs near temporary pools in southeastern Spojené státy.
photos.funFact: Cope's gray tree frogs are nearly identical to gray tree frogs but have a faster trill call. They can survive freezing temperatures by producing antifreeze proteins.

photos.habitat: Rocky potoky and springs in eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Two-lined salamanders have larvae that can take 2-4 let to metamorphose. They are excellent swimmers and can be found under rocks in fast-flowing potoky.

photos.habitat: Sandy areas near water including beaches, fields, and gardens in eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Fowler's toads have a distinctive nasal trill call and can inflate their bodies when threatened. They are excellent diggers and often burrow in sand.

photos.habitat: Deciduous lesy under logs and rocks in eastern Spojené státy.
photos.funFact: Slimy salamanders produce a sticky secretion that is difficult to remove from hands. They are lungless and breathe through their skin and mouth lining.

photos.habitat: rybníky, jezera, and slow potoky across northern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Northern leopard frogs are excellent jumpers and can leap distances up to 20 times their body length. They are commonly used in biology education.

photos.habitat: Caves, springs, and rocky potoky in eastern Spojené státy.
photos.funFact: Long-tailed salamanders have tails that are longer than their body and head combined. They are excellent climbers and can often be found on cave walls.

photos.habitat: Permanent water bodies including rybníky, jezera, and potoky across eastern Severní Amerika.
photos.funFact: Green frogs have a distinctive banjo-like call and prominent ridges running down their backs. Males are territorial and will wrestle with intruders.
